category: Heat Transfer Module: Radiation, Orbital Loads, Lumped Thermal Systems, Moisture Features and Variables
description: Feature nodes and settings of the radiation interfaces (Surface-to-Surface Radiation rad, Radiation in Participating Media rpm, Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media rasm, Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media rbam), the Orbital Thermal Loads interface (otl), the Lumped Thermal System (lts) components, the Moisture Transport (mt) features, and the predefined heat transfer result variables (COMSOL 6.4 Heat Transfer Module).

tools.name: Surface-to-Surface Radiation Methods (Hemicube, Direct Area Integration, Ray Shooting)
tools.description: The Surface-to-Surface Radiation interface computes irradiation with one of three view-factor methods. Hemicube (default) z-buffers the geometry on the faces of a hemicube and handles shadowing (resolution 256, optional adaptive resolution coarsening); Direct area integration is fast and accurate without obstructions but ignores shadowing (integration order 4); Ray shooting (resolution 8) is required for specular reflection, refraction, semitransparent and directional surfaces (Opaque Surface, Specular Mirror, Semitransparent Surface, Dielectric Window, Refractive Interface). In 2D axisymmetry the 2D boundaries are revolved with a set number of azimuthal sectors.
tools.usage: Surface-to-Surface Radiation (rad) > Radiation Settings > Surface-to-surface radiation method. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rad").prop("RadiationSettings").set("radiationMethod", "rayshooting")

parameters.name: radiationMethod
parameters.description: hemicube (default), direct area integration, rayshooting.

parameters.name: radiationResolution / radiationResolutionRayShooting
parameters.description: Hemicube resolution (256) / ray shooting resolution (8).

parameters.name: radiationIntegrationOrder
parameters.description: Direct area integration order (4).

parameters.name: radiationSectors
parameters.description: Azimuthal sectors for 2D axisymmetry.

parameters.name: useRadiationGroups
parameters.description: Enable Radiation Group nodes to speed up computations.

tools.notes: Only ray shooting supports specular reflection, refraction and directional properties; direct area integration does not conserve energy when shadowing exists. Symmetry and external radiation sources work with all methods.

tools.name: Wavelength Dependence of Radiative Properties (Solar and Ambient, Multiple Spectral Bands)
tools.description: Radiation-settings option shared by rad, otl, rpm and rasm. Constant gives a diffuse-gray model; Solar and ambient creates two bands [0, lambda_sol/amb] and [lambda_sol/amb, inf) (default split 2.5 um) so solar absorptivity and IR emissivity can differ; Multiple spectral bands uses a table of right endpoints (vacuum wavelengths) with band-wise properties. Band fractions of blackbody emission (fractional emissive power) are computed from the temperature, and the upper integration bound of the last band defaults to 1 mm.
tools.usage: rad (or rpm/rasm/otl) > Radiation Settings / Participating Media Settings > Wavelength dependence of radiative properties

parameters.name: Separation point lambda_sol/amb
parameters.description: Boundary between solar and ambient bands (2.5[um]).

parameters.name: Right endpoints table + wavelength unit
parameters.description: Band limits for Multiple spectral bands.

parameters.name: Specify the upper bound for integrations
parameters.description: Override lambda_inf = 1[mm].

parameters.name: Weighted sum of gray gases
parameters.description: Additional option in Radiation in Participating Media.

tools.example:
rad > Radiation Settings: Wavelength dependence = Solar and ambient
Diffuse Surface 1 (white paint): emissivity solar band 0.2, ambient band 0.9
External Radiation Source (Solar position) for daytime heating
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Thermal_Radiation/parasol
tools.notes: Band-wise property functions are available as rad.fepsilon(lambda) etc. for checking the values used per band.

tools.name: Opacity (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Domain node that declares domains opaque or transparent for surface-to-surface radiation (optionally per spectral band) and sets their refractive index, which controls on which side of each boundary radiation is emitted when the emitted radiation direction is 'Opacity controlled'. By default all domains and the exterior are transparent; select All voids and set Opaque to close the exterior. With the Heat Transfer with Surface-to-Surface Radiation coupling, solids default to opaque and fluids to transparent.
tools.usage: rad > Domains > Opacity (opac1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rad").create("opac1", "Opacity", 3)

parameters.name: opaqueType
parameters.description: Opaque (1) or Transparent (0); per band for Solar and ambient / Multiple bands.

parameters.name: refractiveIndexConstant
parameters.description: Refractive index of the domain (fallback: default transparent media refractive index).

tools.notes: Ignored on boundaries whose radiation direction is set by normal orientation or both sides, and on Semitransparent Surface boundaries. Variables rad.radopu/rad.radopd indicate opacity on the up/down side.

tools.name: Layer Opacity (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Subnode that defines the in-depth opacity of a boundary representing a thin layer (e.g. a thin glass pane or foil modeled with Thin Layer), independently of the surface opacity used by Diffuse Surface, Diffuse Mirror or Opaque Surface. With several spectral bands the layer can be transparent in some bands (visible) and opaque in others (IR), as needed for greenhouse-type effects.
tools.usage: rad > Diffuse Surface / Opaque Surface > Layer Opacity (lopac1)

parameters.name: Opacity type
parameters.description: Opaque (default) or Transparent, for all or selected wavelengths.

tools.example: rad (Solar and ambient) > Diffuse Surface on the glazing boundary > Layer Opacity: Solar band transparent, Ambient band opaque
tools.notes: Present by default as a hidden node in heat transfer interfaces with radiation.

tools.name: Opaque Surface (Surface-to-Surface Radiation, diffuse and specular)
tools.description: Boundary condition for glossy opaque surfaces that emit diffusely and reflect both diffusely and specularly; available only with the Ray shooting method. Emissivity, diffuse and specular reflectivity can be constant, band-wise or direction dependent (polar and azimuthal angle functions). Use Diffuse Surface when only diffuse reflection matters and Specular Mirror for pure mirrors.
tools.usage: rad > Boundaries > Opaque Surface (osurf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rad").create("osurf1", "OpaqueSurfaceSpecularDiffuse", 1)

parameters.name: epsilon_rad / epsilon_rad_mat
parameters.description: Surface emissivity (from material or user).

parameters.name: Specular reflectivity rho_s
parameters.description: Fraction of reflected radiation that is specular.

parameters.name: directionalDependence
parameters.description: Enable angle-dependent properties.

parameters.name: definePropertyOnEachSide
parameters.description: Different properties up/down side.

tools.notes: No transmission; use Semitransparent Surface for transmitting boundaries.

tools.name: Diffuse Mirror and Specular Mirror (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Two zero-emissivity variants of surface radiation boundaries. Diffuse Mirror (emissivity 0) absorbs all irradiation and re-emits it diffusely - an approximation for well-insulated surfaces with negligible convection - and solves a radiosity variable; Specular Mirror (emissivity and diffuse reflectivity 0, specular reflectivity 1) reflects all irradiation like an ideal mirror, needs the Ray shooting method and needs no radiosity unknown. The net radiative heat flux is zero on both.
tools.usage: rad > Boundaries > Diffuse Mirror | Specular Mirror (Specular Mirror only with Ray shooting).

parameters.name: Radiation direction
parameters.description: Opacity controlled, normal direction, or both sides (as for Diffuse Surface).

parameters.name: Ambient
parameters.description: Ambient temperature seen through openings.

tools.example: Solar concentrator: rad (Ray shooting) > Specular Mirror on the reflector boundaries; Diffuse Surface on the absorber tube; External Radiation Source at infinite distance
tools.notes: Specular Mirror replaces the radiosity shape function by zero, reducing the number of unknowns.

tools.name: Semitransparent Surface (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Ray-shooting boundary condition for surfaces that emit, reflect (diffusely and specularly) and transmit radiation specularly, with refraction between domains of different refractive index computed by Snell's law. Directional dependence of reflection, transmission and emission can be user defined. Radiation occurs on both sides of the surface, and Opacity nodes are ignored on it.
tools.usage: rad (Ray shooting) > Boundaries > Semitransparent Surface

parameters.name: Emissivity, diffuse reflectivity
parameters.description: Diffuse properties of the surface.

parameters.name: Specular reflectivity, specular transmissivity
parameters.description: Specular properties; may depend on angle.

parameters.name: Refractive indices
parameters.description: From adjacent domains (Opacity nodes).

tools.example: Greenhouse panel: rad (Ray shooting, Solar and ambient) > Semitransparent Surface on the polycarbonate sheet: solar transmissivity 0.8, IR transmissivity 0
tools.notes: Use Refractive Interface for pure Fresnel reflection/transmission and Dielectric Window for absorbing thin dielectric layers.

tools.name: Dielectric Window and Refractive Interface (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Ray-shooting boundaries whose directional properties come from Fresnel relations. Dielectric Window models a thin dielectric layer with refractive index and absorption coefficient (Beer-Lambert absorption, absorbed energy re-emitted as gray-body radiation on both sides), giving directional emissivity, specular reflectivity and transmissivity. Refractive Interface models a sharp interface between domains of different refractive index with only specular reflection and transmission (no radiosity unknown).
tools.usage: rad (Ray shooting) > Boundaries > Dielectric Window | Refractive Interface. For speed set Angular dependent properties = Interpolated function in the interface settings.

parameters.name: Refractive index, absorption coefficient, thickness
parameters.description: Dielectric Window layer properties.

parameters.name: angularDependentProperties
parameters.description: full (default) or interpolated function.

tools.example: Vacuum viewport of a furnace: rad (Ray shooting) > Dielectric Window on the quartz pane (n = 1.45, absorption coefficient 5[1/m], thickness 5[mm])
tools.notes: Both are variants of Semitransparent Surface; radiation on both sides.

tools.name: Radiation Shield (Surface-to-Surface Radiation, multilayer insulation)
tools.description: Boundary node modeling the thermal resistance of one or several radiative insulation layers (multilayer insulation, MLI, radiation shields) without geometry: shield type and radiative properties are set separately on the Radiation Shield, Upside and Downside default subnodes. It can be applied only where Diffuse Surface or Opaque Surface is used and, with a heat-transfer coupling, only on external boundaries of the heat interface; shield temperatures are available as rad.Tshieldu / rad.Tshieldd.
tools.usage: rad > Boundaries > Radiation Shield (with subnodes Radiation Shield, Upside and Radiation Shield, Downside)

parameters.name: Number of shields and shield emissivities
parameters.description: Define the MLI stack per side.

parameters.name: Shield type
parameters.description: Set independently on upside and downside (specular properties with ray shooting).

tools.example: Spacecraft panel: rad/otl > Diffuse Surface on outer panel + Radiation Shield (10 layers, emissivity 0.03) to model MLI blankets
tools.notes: Heat Flux and Deposited Beam Power on such boundaries act on the outermost shield temperature.

tools.name: Prescribed Radiosity (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Boundary condition that prescribes the radiosity leaving a surface - blackbody radiation at a temperature, graybody radiation with an emissivity, or a user-defined expression - for each spectral band. The prescribed radiosity does not affect the boundary itself but defines how it irradiates others, e.g. a heater lamp or a hot furnace wall modeled only as a radiation emitter.
tools.usage: rad > Boundaries > Prescribed Radiosity

parameters.name: Radiosity expression
parameters.description: Blackbody, Graybody (emissivity + temperature) or user defined J0.

parameters.name: Radiation direction
parameters.description: As for Diffuse Surface.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Boundary system for directional properties (ray shooting).

tools.example: rad > Prescribed Radiosity on lamp filament boundary: Graybody radiation, epsilon = 0.35, T = 2800[K]
tools.notes: Directional dependence only with Ray shooting.

tools.name: Radiation Group (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Node that gathers radiative boundaries that can see each other into separate groups so that view factors are computed only within groups, which speeds up large radiation models. By default all boundaries of Diffuse Surface, Diffuse Mirror and Prescribed Radiosity belong to one group; enable 'Use radiation groups' to add groups, and a boundary moved to a manual group leaves the default one.
tools.usage: rad > Radiation Settings > select Use radiation groups; then rad > Radiation Group

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Boundaries that mutually see each other.

tools.example: Two separate enclosures in one model: rad > Radiation Group 1 (enclosure A boundaries), Radiation Group 2 (enclosure B boundaries)
tools.notes: In 2D axisymmetry group according to the revolved 3D geometry, not the 2D view.

tools.name: External Radiation Source (Surface-to-Surface Radiation, point, directional and solar)
tools.description: Global node adding direct irradiation from an external source to all Diffuse Surface, Diffuse Mirror, Opaque Surface, Specular Mirror and Semitransparent Surface boundaries: a point source at x_s radiating uniformly, a source at infinite distance with incident direction i_s, or (3D) the Sun computed from Solar position (location by coordinates, city, or an Ambient Properties weather station; date, time, time zone and daylight saving). Only external view factors are recomputed when the source moves; source power can be blackbody at T_s = 5780 K or user defined.
tools.usage: rad > Global > External Radiation Source (ers1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rad").create("ers1", "ExternalRadiationSource", -1)

parameters.name: sourcePosition
parameters.description: Point coordinate, InfiniteDistance, SolarPosition.

parameters.name: xs / is
parameters.description: Source location or incident radiation direction.

parameters.name: Ps / q0s
parameters.description: Source power (point) or incident flux (directional); or blackbody at TsCoord/TsInf.

parameters.name: locationType, city, LatitudeToNorth, LongitudeToEast, Day, Month, Hour, TimeZone, UpdateTimeFromSolver
parameters.description: Solar position inputs.

tools.notes: Only direct irradiation; diffuse sky radiation is controlled by 'Include diffuse radiation' in Diffuse Surface/Diffuse Mirror Ambient settings. North, west, up correspond to x, y, z.

tools.name: Symmetry for Surface-to-Surface Radiation
tools.description: Global node that lets view factors be computed on only part of a symmetric geometry: one symmetry plane (2D, 2D axisymmetric, 3D), two or three perpendicular planes, sector symmetry (2D, 3D) and sectors with a reflection plane. Radiation from the modeled part is mirrored or rotated so that the full enclosure is accounted for, reducing cost substantially.
tools.usage: rad > Global > Symmetry for Surface-to-Surface Radiation (rsym1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rad").create("rsym1", "SymmetryForSurfaceToSurfaceRadiation", -1)

parameters.name: typeOfSymmetry
parameters.description: Plane symmetry, two/three perpendicular planes (ThreePerpendicularSymmetryPlanes), SectorSymmetry, sectors with reflection.

parameters.name: numberOfSectors, planes definition
parameters.description: Sector count and plane points/normals.

parameters.name: applySymERS
parameters.description: Also apply symmetry to external radiation sources.

tools.notes: Combine with thermal Symmetry conditions in the heat transfer interface on the same planes.

tools.name: Fluence Rate Calculation (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Domain node that computes the fluence rate - total radiant power hitting a small sphere divided by its cross section - inside transparent domains from the surface radiosities, stored at Gauss points for fast evaluation. The variable is rad.E0 (and rad.E0_band<k> per band), used for UV disinfection, photoreactors and irradiance mapping.
tools.usage: rad > Domains > Fluence Rate Calculation; evaluate rad.E0 in results.

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Transparent domains where the fluence rate is evaluated.

parameters.name: Gauss point order
parameters.description: Set in the Discretization section of the interface.

tools.example:
rad > Fluence Rate Calculation 1 on the air domain of a UV cabinet
Results > 3D Plot > Slice: rad.E0 (W/m^2)
tools.notes: Ray Optics has a similar Fluence Rate Calculation node (gop).

tools.name: Radiosity, Irradiation and View Factor Variables (Surface-to-Surface Radiation)
tools.description: Result quantities of the radiosity method (J = epsilon*e_b(T) + rho_d*G, irradiation G = G_m + F_amb*e_b(T_amb) + G_ext): surface radiosity rad.J (and rad.Ju/rad.Jd for upside/downside), mutual irradiation rad.Gm, radiative net heat flux rad.rflux, blackbody emissive power rad.ebu, surface emissivity rad.epsilon, opacity indicators rad.radopu/rad.radopd, and shield temperatures rad.Tshieldu/d. F_amb is the ambient view factor (fraction of the view that sees the ambient).
tools.usage: Results > any plot or Derived Value with expressions rad.J, rad.Ju, rad.Gm, rad.rflux ...; heat side: ht.rflux (radiative heat flux in ht).

parameters.name: rad.J / rad.Ju / rad.Jd
parameters.description: Surface radiosity (W/m^2).

parameters.name: rad.Gm
parameters.description: Mutual surface irradiation.

parameters.name: rad.rflux
parameters.description: Net radiative heat flux.

parameters.name: rad.E0
parameters.description: Fluence rate (with Fluence Rate Calculation).

tools.notes: View factor theory: 'View Factor Evaluation' and 'The Radiosity Method for Diffuse-Gray Surfaces' in the Heat Transfer Module User's Guide.

tools.name: Surface Property Functions (Surface-to-Surface Radiation, rad.fepsilon)
tools.description: Predefined functions that return the wavelength dependence of surface properties actually used for each band when Solar and ambient or Multiple spectral bands is active: emissivity (fepsilon), diffuse reflectivity (frho_d), specular reflectivity (frho_s), specular transmissivity (ftau_s), refractive index (fnIndex) and critical angle (ftheta_rad). Variants are physics averaged (rad.fepsilon(lambda)), piecewise constant (rad.fepsilon_const), feature averaged (rad.dsurf1.fepsilon), and locally evaluated (rad.fepsilon_at(x,y,z,lambda), rad.fepsilon_atconst).
tools.usage: Results > 1D Plot Group > Global/Function plot with expression rad.fepsilon(lambda) over a wavelength range; similar rpm.fepsilon for participating media.

parameters.name: lambda
parameters.description: Vacuum wavelength argument.

parameters.name: x,y,z
parameters.description: Evaluation point for the *_at variants.

tools.example: Results > 1D Plot Group > Function: rad.fepsilon(lambda) and rad.fepsilon_const(lambda) for lambda = range(0.2[um], 0.05[um], 20[um]) to compare the material emissivity curve with the banded values
tools.notes: Feature-averaged functions exist for Dielectric Window, Diffuse Mirror, Diffuse Surface, Opaque Surface, Semitransparent Surface and similar features.

tools.name: Participating Medium (Radiation in Participating Media)
tools.description: Domain node of the rpm interface for absorbing, emitting and scattering media: it solves the radiative transfer equation (DOM) or the P1 equation for the incident radiation G, and provides the heat source Q = kappa*(G - 4*pi*I_b(T)) to a coupled heat interface. Properties are absorption coefficient kappa, scattering coefficient sigma_s and a scattering phase function (ScatteringType Isotropic, LinearAnisotropic with coefficient a1, or higher-order/other forms using a1..a12 and eta), per spectral band if needed.
tools.usage: rpm > Participating Medium (rpm1 default). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rpm").create("rpm2", "ParticipatingMedium", 3)

parameters.name: kappaR / kappaR_mat
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient (from material or user).

parameters.name: sigmaS / sigmaS_mat
parameters.description: Scattering coefficient.

parameters.name: ScatteringType
parameters.description: Isotropic, LinearAnisotropic, polynomial or other phase functions (a1..., eta).

parameters.name: NormalizePhaseFunction
parameters.description: Normalize a user phase function.

tools.notes: Incident radiation variable rpm.G; net boundary flux rpm.qr_net.

tools.name: Discrete Ordinates Method and P1 Approximation (Radiation in Participating Media)
tools.description: Radiation discretization methods of rpm and rasm. The discrete ordinates method (default in 2D/3D) solves one intensity per direction of an S_N quadrature (Level Symmetric Even, Level Symmetric Hybrid, Equal Weight Odd: S2/S4/S6/S8 give 8/24/48/80 directions in 3D) or a T_N quasi-uniform weight set (8N^2 directions); the P1 approximation (default in 2D axisymmetry) solves a single diffusion-type equation for G and is much cheaper but less accurate for optically thin media. A reduced Jacobian option and inconsistent stabilization help DOM convergence.
tools.usage: rpm > Participating Media Settings > Radiation discretization method. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rpm").prop("ParticipatingMediaSettingsProperty").set("nrad", "nr")

parameters.name: RadiationDiscretizationMethod
parameters.description: DiscreteOrdinateMethod or P1Approximation.

parameters.name: QuadratureSet / DiscreteOrdinatesMethod
parameters.description: LevelSymmetricEven (default), LSH, EWO, quasi-uniform; order S2-S16.

parameters.name: nrad
parameters.description: Refractive index of the participating media.

parameters.name: Use reduced Jacobian
parameters.description: Default on; lowers memory for many directions.

tools.example:
rpm > Participating Media Settings: Radiation discretization method = Discrete ordinates method, Quadrature set = Level symmetric even, S6
// Compare Heat_Transfer_Module/Verification_Examples/cylinder_participating_media (DOM) and cylinder_participating_media_p1 (P1)
tools.notes: With DOM, Opaque Surface and Continuity on Interior Boundary are default nodes; with P1 only Opaque Surface, and Incident Intensity is available.

tools.name: Weighted Sum of Gray Gases Model (Radiation in Participating Media)
tools.description: Wavelength-dependence option of rpm for combustion gases (H2O/CO2 mixtures): radiation is represented by a transparent gas plus several gray gases, each with its own absorption coefficient and temperature-dependent weight factor (user defined or polynomial expansion up to order 5, optionally normalized with a reference temperature); the RTE is solved for each gray gas. It captures non-gray gas radiation in furnaces and boilers at moderate cost.
tools.usage: rpm > Participating Media Settings > Wavelength dependence of radiative properties = Weighted sum of gray gases model; fill the absorption coefficient and weight factor tables.

parameters.name: numberOfGasesWSGG
parameters.description: Number of gray gases (plus the transparent gas).

parameters.name: kappaRWSGG
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient of each gray gas.

parameters.name: Weight factors
parameters.description: User defined or polynomial expansion coefficients (b0WSGG, b1WSGG ...).

tools.example:
rpm (Discrete ordinates method) > Participating Media Settings > Wavelength dependence = Weighted sum of gray gases model
Number of gray gases = 3 (+ transparent gas); enter kappa_i and polynomial weight-factor coefficients for an H2O/CO2 combustion mixture
Couple with htrpm1 to the heat transfer interface of the furnace gas
tools.notes: The first gas is transparent (kappa = 0) and its weight is deduced so that weights sum to 1.

tools.name: Opaque Surface and Semitransparent Surface (Radiation in Participating Media)
tools.description: Boundary conditions of rpm/rasm. Opaque Surface prescribes the incident intensities from wall emission and reflection and computes the absorbed net radiative flux q_r,net (wall types: gray wall with emissivity, or infinite/black wall); it is a default node (wall types GrayWall, BlackWall, InfiniteWall). Semitransparent Surface (DOM only) additionally models diffuse and specular transmission through the boundary, e.g. a window separating two media.
tools.usage: rpm > Boundaries > Opaque Surface (os1 default) | Semitransparent Surface. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("rpm").create("os2", "OpaqueSurface", 2)

parameters.name: WallType
parameters.description: GrayWall (emissivity epsilon_rad), BlackWall or InfiniteWall.

parameters.name: Fractional emissive power
parameters.description: Per band for spectral models.

parameters.name: Transmissivity (semitransparent)
parameters.description: Diffuse and specular transmission fractions.

tools.notes: Results: rpm.qr_net, rpm.qr_out.

tools.name: Incident Intensity (Radiation in Participating Media)
tools.description: Boundary condition of rpm and rasm prescribing the radiative intensity along incoming directions (outgoing ones are free): user-defined external intensity, or blackbody / graybody radiation at an external temperature (rpm only), per spectral band. Use it for openings, windows and illuminated inlets of semitransparent domains.
tools.usage: rpm or rasm > Boundaries > Incident Intensity (P1 or DOM; pair version from the Pairs menu).

parameters.name: External radiation intensity I_ext
parameters.description: User defined, Blackbody radiation I_b(T_ext) or Graybody epsilon*I_b(T_ext).

parameters.name: T_ext
parameters.description: External temperature (293.15 K default).

tools.example: rasm > Incident Intensity on the illuminated face of a tissue phantom: I_ext = P_lamp/(pi*A_spot)
tools.notes: For collimated laser beams prefer Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media.

tools.name: Radiative Source (Radiation in Participating Media)
tools.description: Domain node adding a radiative power source Q0 inside a participating medium: with P1 it is added to the equation for G, with DOM it is divided by 4*pi as a directional source in the RTE; band-wise sources are possible with spectral models. Useful for luminescent volumes, radioactive or chemiluminescent sources, or lamps modeled as volumes.
tools.usage: rpm > Domains > Radiative Source

parameters.name: Radiative source type
parameters.description: Power density Q0 or other available forms; per band Q0,k.

parameters.name: Material type
parameters.description: Solid (material frame) or nonsolid (spatial frame).

tools.example: rpm > Radiative Source on the plasma column domain: power density Q0 = P_rad/V_plasma
tools.notes: Available for Constant, Solar and ambient, and Multiple spectral bands wavelength dependence.

tools.name: Absorbing-Scattering Medium (Radiation in Absorbing-Scattering Media)
tools.description: Domain node of rasm for nonemitting semitransparent media: absorption coefficient kappa, scattering coefficient sigma_s and phase function define the RTE without emission (DOM) or the P1 equation for G, and the absorbed power Q_r = kappa*G is available as a heat source through the htrasm coupling. Suited to light diffusion in biological tissue, milk-like liquids, aerogels or phosphor layers.
tools.usage: rasm > Absorbing-Scattering Medium (default domain node)

parameters.name: kappa
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient (1/m).

parameters.name: sigma_s
parameters.description: Scattering coefficient (1/m).

parameters.name: Scattering phase function
parameters.description: Isotropic, linear anisotropic, polynomial, Henyey-Greenstein-type.

tools.example: rasm (P1) > Absorbing-Scattering Medium: kappa = 0.3[1/cm], sigma_s = 100[1/cm] (skin at 800 nm); htrasm1 coupling to Bioheat Transfer
tools.notes: Use Participating Medium (rpm) when the medium emits thermal radiation.

tools.name: Absorbing Medium and Incident Intensity (Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media)
tools.description: Nodes of rbam. Absorbing Medium solves the Beer-Lambert equation e_i.grad(I_i) = -kappa*I_i for each beam and deposits Q = sum(kappa*I_i) as heat; Incident Intensity defines each beam by orientation e and profile - built-in Gaussian (power P0, origin O, standard deviation sigma) or top-hat disk (radius R, smoothing dR) - or a user beam power density I0, applied on boundaries where e.n < 0. Transparent Surface (default) and Opaque Surface set the exit conditions.
tools.usage: rbam > Absorbing Medium (default) ; rbam > Boundaries > Incident Intensity | Opaque Surface | Transparent Surface

parameters.name: kappa
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient of the medium.

parameters.name: e, P0, O, sigma / R
parameters.description: Beam orientation, power, origin and profile width.

parameters.name: I0
parameters.description: User-defined beam power density (W/m^2).

tools.example:
rbam > Incident Intensity 1: e = (0,0,-1), Gaussian, P0 = 10[W], O = (x0+v*t, 0, H), sigma = 0.25[mm]
rbam > Absorbing Medium 1: kappa = 20[1/cm]
Multiphysics: htrbam1 to Heat Transfer in Solids
tools.notes: Multiple beams require one Incident Intensity per beam. No scattering or emission is modeled.

tools.name: Orbital Parameters (Orbital Thermal Loads)
tools.description: Global otl node defining the spacecraft orbit: Elliptical (six Keplerian elements: semimajor axis, eccentricity, inclination, longitude of ascending node or local time at ascending node, argument of periapsis, true anomaly at start), Equatorial elliptical, Circular (orbit radius, inclination, ascending node), Equatorial circular, or User defined trajectory from functions or data (X, Y, Z in the Earth-centered system).
tools.usage: otl > Orbital Parameters (op1, default). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("otl").feature("op1").set("orbitType", "circular")

parameters.name: orbitType
parameters.description: elliptical, equatorial elliptical, circular, equatorial circular, user defined.

parameters.name: a_orbit / R_orbit, e_orbit, i_orbit
parameters.description: Semimajor axis or radius (default otl.R_planet+1000[km]), eccentricity, inclination.

parameters.name: omegaType
parameters.description: loan (longitude of ascending node) or ltan (local time at ascending node, omegaTime_orbit).

parameters.name: omegaPeriapsis_orbit, nu0_orbit
parameters.description: Argument of periapsis and true anomaly at start.

tools.notes: Orbital period available as otl.T_orbit.

tools.name: Planet Properties (Orbital Thermal Loads)
tools.description: Global otl node with planet mass, radius, tilt, rotation rate and initial longitude (from GMT at start time, the subspacecraft point or the vernal point), plus planet radiative properties: albedo and planet infrared flux, constant or dependent on geographic position (user distributions or functions, per spectral band). Earth is predefined (5.972e24 kg, 6378 km, 23.45 deg tilt, 24 h rotation).
tools.usage: otl > Planet Properties (plp1, default). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("otl").feature("plp1").set("longType", "spacecraft")

parameters.name: planetProperties
parameters.description: earth (default) or user defined (M_planet, R_planet, tilt_planet, rot_planet).

parameters.name: longType
parameters.description: gmt, spacecraft (longitude at subspacecraft point), vernal point.

parameters.name: planetAlbedoTypeSolAmb / planetAlbedoSolAmb
parameters.description: Albedo definition (e.g. userdefDistribution, 0.3).

parameters.name: planetRadiativeFluxTypeSolAmb
parameters.description: Planet IR flux definition.

tools.notes: The planet is discretized in rings for albedo/IR view factors (nRings, nPointsRing).

tools.name: Sun Properties (Orbital Thermal Loads)
tools.description: Global otl node defining the Sun direction and solar flux: predefined Winter solstice (1414 W/m^2), Summer solstice (1322 W/m^2), Spring and Fall equinox (1367 W/m^2) with the corresponding Sun vector, or a user-defined Sun vector in the Earth-centered system. With Automatic solar flux a 5780 K blackbody spectrum is used for spectral bands; user-defined and per-band fluxes are possible.
tools.usage: otl > Sun Properties (sup1, default)

parameters.name: sunDirection
parameters.description: winterSol, summer solstice, spring/fall equinox, or user defined (SV_ECS).

parameters.name: Solar flux
parameters.description: Automatic, User defined, User defined per band (q0s...).

parameters.name: TsInf
parameters.description: Sun blackbody temperature (5780 K).

tools.example: otl > Sun Properties 1: Sun direction = Summer solstice (1322 W/m^2), Solar flux = Automatic
tools.notes: Global variables otl.SVX_ECS, otl.SVY_ECS, otl.SVZ_ECS give the Sun vector; otl.isIlluminated flags eclipse.

tools.name: Spacecraft Axes and Spacecraft Orientation (Orbital Thermal Loads)
tools.description: Attitude definition of the Orbital Thermal Loads interface. Spacecraft Axes defines primary and secondary body axes (from a surface selection's averaged normal, +X, +Y or user vector; the third axis is their cross product). Spacecraft Orientation points the primary axis to Nadir, Zenith, Sun, Anti-Sun, Velocity, Antivelocity or other targets, aligns the secondary axis, and optionally adds spin about the axes (rate or angular position). Several Axes/Orientation pairs can be switched in the Events Timeline.
tools.usage: otl > Spacecraft Axes (sa1) and Spacecraft Orientation (so1), both default. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("otl").feature("so1").set("primaryRotation", "rate")

parameters.name: primaryOrientation / secondaryOrientation
parameters.description: nadir (default), zenith, sun, anti-sun, velocity (secondary default), antivelocity, ...

parameters.name: primaryRotation, primaryAngularRate
parameters.description: Spin about the primary axis, e.g. 2*360[deg]/otl.T_orbit.

parameters.name: Primary / Secondary axis (Axes)
parameters.description: From primary selection, +X, +Y or user defined.

tools.notes: An error is raised if primary and secondary axes are collinear.

tools.name: Events Timeline, Implicit Event and Ground Pointing (Orbital Thermal Loads)
tools.description: Event management of the Orbital Thermal Loads interface. Events Timeline (default) sets the initial axes/orientation and fast tumbling state and a table of implicit and explicit events that switch attitude or tumbling during the orbit; Implicit Event defines user events by an indicator expression crossing an upper or lower threshold; Ground Pointing points at a ground station (coordinates or an ASHRAE station) with triggers on elevation angle or ranging. The obsolete Generate Events Interface (pre-6.2) is replaced by Events Timeline.
tools.usage: otl > Events Timeline (et1) ; otl > Global > Implicit Event | Ground Pointing

parameters.name: initFastTumbling
parameters.description: Start with the fast tumbling approximation (averaged solar loads, no external view factors).

parameters.name: initAxesFeature / initOrientationFeature
parameters.description: Initial Spacecraft Axes and Orientation nodes (sa1, so1).

parameters.name: Event table
parameters.description: Event type, start, period, axes/orientation to activate.

parameters.name: Event indicator, threshold
parameters.description: Implicit event definition.

tools.example:
otl > Events Timeline 1: row 1 Ground Pointing 1 (elevation > 10 deg) -> switch to Spacecraft Orientation 2 (antenna to station)
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Orbital_Thermal_Loads/orbit_calculation
tools.notes: Only one active Events Timeline is expected when solving.

tools.name: Conductive Thermal Resistor (Lumped Thermal System)
tools.description: Two-port passive component (prefix R) of the Lumped Thermal System relating the heat rate P to the temperature difference between its nodes by P = dT/R. R is entered directly or computed from conductivity and geometry (plane shell, cylindrical shell, spherical shell with area, thickness or radii), optionally including natural convection enhancement (Nusselt correlations) or radiation in an optically thick medium.
tools.usage: lts > Conductive Thermal Resistor. Java: model.component("comp2").physics("lts").create("R1", "ConductiveThermalResistor", -1)

parameters.name: Connections
parameters.description: Node names of ports p1 and p2.

parameters.name: resistorType
parameters.description: ThermalResistance (R) or GeometricProperties (geomConfig PlaneShell ..., A, L, r_i, r_o, k).

parameters.name: Temperature model input
parameters.description: Default average of port temperatures 0.5*(lts.Tp1+lts.Tp2) for T-dependent k.

tools.notes: Component variables are scoped like lts.R1.<variable>; the Lumped Thermal System interface is created with physics().create("lts", "LumpedThermalSystem", "geom1").

tools.name: Convective Thermal Resistor (Lumped Thermal System)
tools.description: Two-port component (prefix CR) modeling convection between a solid wall node p1 and a fluid node p2 with R_conv = 1/(h*A); h is user defined or taken from the same external/internal natural and forced convection correlations as the Heat Flux boundary condition, with the wall temperature used as model input.
tools.usage: lts > Convective Thermal Resistor

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Surface area of the convective exchange.

parameters.name: h / correlation
parameters.description: User defined or External/Internal natural/forced convection with fluid and geometry inputs.

parameters.name: Ports
parameters.description: p1 = solid wall, p2 = fluid.

tools.example: lts > Convective Thermal Resistor CR1 between node 'case' and node 'air': A = 0.01[m^2], External natural convection, Vertical wall, L = 5[cm]
tools.notes: For a convective loss to a fixed ambient at a single node, use Heat Rate with Convective heat rate instead.

tools.name: Radiative Thermal Resistor and Radiative Heat Rate (Lumped Thermal System)
tools.description: Radiation components of the Lumped Thermal System. Radiative Thermal Resistor (prefix RR) is a two-port component for radiative exchange between two opaque diffuse gray surfaces in an enclosure (radiative resistance from emissivities, areas and view factor configuration). Radiative Heat Rate is a one-port node applying surface-to-ambient radiation P = epsilon*sigma*A*(T_amb^4 - T^4), expressed through an equivalent radiative resistance.
tools.usage: lts > Radiative Thermal Resistor | Radiative Heat Rate

parameters.name: Emissivities, areas, configuration
parameters.description: Radiative Thermal Resistor inputs.

parameters.name: A, epsilon, T_amb
parameters.description: Radiative Heat Rate inputs (emissivity from material or user).

tools.example: lts > Radiative Heat Rate on node 'radiator': A = 0.5[m^2], epsilon = 0.85, T_amb = 3[K] (deep space)
tools.notes: Radiative resistances are temperature dependent; stationary solves are nonlinear.

tools.name: Thermal Capacitor and Thermal Mass (Lumped Thermal System)
tools.description: Heat storage components. Thermal Capacitor (prefix C) is a two-port component with P = C*d(dT)/dt between its ports; Thermal Mass is a one-port node with a virtual fixed-temperature reference, P = C*dT/dt. The capacitance C is given directly or computed as rho*V*Cp or m*Cp. In stationary studies P = 0.
tools.usage: lts > Thermal Capacitor | Thermal Mass

parameters.name: Specify
parameters.description: Thermal capacitance C, or volume/density/heat capacity, or mass/heat capacity.

parameters.name: Initial temperature
parameters.description: Initial node temperature(s) for transient runs.

tools.example: lts > Thermal Mass on node 'battery': m = 0.8[kg], Cp = 900[J/(kg*K)]; Heat Rate source P0 = 5[W]; Conductive Thermal Resistor to 'case'
tools.notes: Thermal Mass is the usual choice for lumped bodies; Thermal Capacitor models storage between two nodes.

tools.name: Heat Rate, Heat Rate Source and Temperature (Lumped Thermal System)
tools.description: Source and boundary components of the Lumped Thermal System. Heat Rate is a one-port node with prescribed P0 or a Convective heat rate (with correlations), Nucleate boiling heat rate or Joule heating option; Heat Rate Source (prefix P) is a two-port source imposing P_src between two nodes; Temperature is a one-port node fixing the node temperature T0. Nucleate Boiling Heat Rate (prefix NBP) is a two-port sink using the Rohsenow correlation.
tools.usage: lts > Heat Rate | Heat Rate Source | Temperature | Nucleate Boiling Heat Rate

parameters.name: Heat Rate > Specify
parameters.description: Heat rate, Convective heat rate, Nucleate boiling heat rate, Joule heating.

parameters.name: P_src
parameters.description: Heat rate of the two-port source.

parameters.name: T0
parameters.description: Prescribed node temperature.

tools.example:
lts > Temperature T_amb (node 'ambient', T0 = 298.15[K])
lts > Heat Rate Source P1 between 'ambient' and 'chip': P_src = 12[W]
Results: node temperatures and heat rates added to default plots
tools.notes: Default results include heat rate and node temperatures for each component.

tools.name: External Terminal (Lumped Thermal System)
tools.description: One-port component that connects a node of the thermal network to a finite-element model: it receives the temperature from a Lumped System Connector boundary (or a shell interface/edge connector) and returns the heat rate the network draws, which the connector applies as a heat flux. The External Connection section reports whether the terminal is connected.
tools.usage: lts > External Terminal (term1). Java: model.component("comp2").physics("lts").create("term1", "ExternalTerminal", -1)

parameters.name: Node name
parameters.description: Network node attached to the FEM boundary.

parameters.name: T_init
parameters.description: Initial temperature (used by the connector in transient runs).

parameters.name: includeHeatRate / includeTemperature
parameters.description: Add to default results.

tools.notes: The Lumped Thermal System can live in a 0D component or in the same component as the FEM model.

tools.name: Heat Pipe and Thermoelectric Module (Lumped Thermal System)
tools.description: Device-level components of the Lumped Thermal System. Heat Pipe is a two-port passive component between evaporator and condenser nodes with a total resistance given directly or built from wall and wick conduction resistances (heat rate set to zero if the condenser is hotter). Thermoelectric Module is a two-port source modeling a Peltier module: port heat rates include the Peltier term S*I*T, half the Joule heating I^2*R_e, conduction through the thermocouples and heat storage.
tools.usage: lts > Heat Pipe | Thermoelectric Module

parameters.name: Heat Pipe: R or wall/wick geometry and properties
parameters.description: Total thermal resistance of the pipe.

parameters.name: Thermoelectric Module: S, R_e, K, I, number of couples
parameters.description: Seebeck coefficient, electrical resistance, thermal conductance, operating current.

tools.example: lts: node 'cold_plate' - Thermoelectric Module TE1 (S = 0.05[V/K], I = 3[A], R_e = 1.5[ohm]) - node 'hot_side' - Conductive Thermal Resistor (heat sink) - Temperature (ambient)
tools.notes: For detailed thermoelectric FEM models use the Thermoelectric Effect multiphysics coupling (Applications/thermoelectric_cooler).

tools.name: Subsystem Definition and Subsystem Instance (Lumped Thermal System)
tools.description: Hierarchical network tools: Subsystem Definition groups components into a reusable subnetwork with ordered connecting node names; Subsystem Instance (prefix X) inserts an instance of a defined subsystem into the main network or another subsystem by mapping its node names.
tools.usage: lts > Subsystem Definition (add components as subnodes) ; lts > Subsystem Instance (Name of subsystem link + node mapping)

parameters.name: Node names (definition)
parameters.description: External nodes of the subsystem, in order.

parameters.name: Name of subsystem link
parameters.description: Which definition the instance uses.

tools.example:
lts > Subsystem Definition 'fin_stack' (nodes base, tip) containing Conductive/Convective resistors
lts > Subsystem Instance X1 and X2 of 'fin_stack' connected to 'chip' and 'ambient'
tools.notes: Components inside a subsystem may connect only to subsystem nodes and each other.

tools.name: Moist Air (Moisture Transport domain node)
tools.description: Domain node of the Moisture Transport interfaces for vapor diffusion and convection in air. For low vapor concentration a diluted-species formulation transports the vapor concentration c_v = phi_w*c_sat (air density unaffected); for larger concentrations a concentrated-species formulation (mixture type) includes density variations and compressibility. Turbulent Mixing can be added for RANS velocity fields and a Moisture Source for volumetric generation.
tools.usage: Moisture Transport in Air (mt) > Moist Air 1 (ma1). Java (mixture type): model.component("comp1").physics("mt").prop("PhysicalModelProperty").set("MixtureType", "ConcentratedSpecies")

parameters.name: Velocity field u, absolute pressure
parameters.description: From a flow interface or user defined.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Vapor diffusion coefficient in air (from material or built-in).

parameters.name: MixtureType (interface)
parameters.description: DilutedSpecies or ConcentratedSpecies.

tools.notes: Moist-air helper variables: mt.fpsat (saturation pressure function), mt.G_evap (evaporation source).

tools.name: Wet Surface and Moist Surface (Moisture Transport, evaporation and condensation)
tools.description: Boundary conditions for evaporation/condensation on solid surfaces adjacent to moist air or a hygroscopic porous medium. Wet Surface assumes a surface fully covered with liquid water: g_evap = M_v*K*(c_sat - c_v) with evaporation rate factor K. Moist Surface handles a partially wet surface by solving for the liquid water concentration c_l accumulated on the surface (condensation film builds up and dries out). Both provide the latent heat source L_v*g_evap to the Heat and Moisture coupling.
tools.usage: mt > Boundaries > Wet Surface (ws1) | Moist Surface (msu1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("mt").create("ws1", "WetSurface", 2); ...create("msu1", "MoistSurface", 1)

parameters.name: K
parameters.description: Evaporation rate factor (m/s); large values approach equilibrium.

parameters.name: Initial liquid water concentration (Moist Surface)
parameters.description: c_l at t = 0.

parameters.name: Include latent heat source on surfaces (ham coupling)
parameters.description: Adds L_v*g_evap to the heat equation.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("mt").create("ws1", "WetSurface", 2);
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Phase_Change/evaporative_cooling (Wet Surface), Power_Electronics_and_Electronic_Cooling/condensation_electronic_device_transport_diffusion (Moist Surface)
tools.notes: Applicable on exterior boundaries of Moist Air or Hygroscopic Porous Medium (equilibrium formulation) domains.

tools.name: Building Material (Moisture Transport in Building Materials)
tools.description: Domain node solving the relative humidity equation xi*d(phi_w)/dt + div(-xi*D_w*grad(phi_w) - delta_p*grad(phi_w*p_sat)) = G for building materials, with moisture storage capacity xi from the sorption isotherm, moisture (liquid) diffusivity D_w and vapor permeability delta_p (or vapor resistance factor). Temperature and pressure are model inputs, normally from Heat Transfer in Building Materials.
tools.usage: Moisture Transport in Building Materials (mt) > Building Material 1 (bm1)

parameters.name: Moisture storage function w(phi_w)
parameters.description: Sorption curve (from Building library material).

parameters.name: D_w
parameters.description: Moisture diffusivity (liquid transport).

parameters.name: delta_p / mu
parameters.description: Vapor permeability or vapor resistance factor.

tools.example:
mt > Building Material 1: material 'Gypsum board' (Building library), temperature from ht
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Verification_Examples/semi_infinite_wall (moisture storage function from file)
tools.notes: Designed for building materials; use Hygroscopic Porous Medium for other porous media.

tools.name: Hygroscopic Porous Medium (Moisture Transport)
tools.description: Domain node for porous media filled with liquid water and moist air, transporting vapor by diffusion and convection and liquid by convection and capillary flow. With the Equilibrium formulation a moisture storage function links relative humidity and liquid saturation (single equation, evaporation stored in mt.G_evap); with the Nonequilibrium formulation liquid saturation and relative humidity are solved separately with an evaporation rate. Subnodes Moist Air, Liquid Water and Porous Matrix hold phase properties; gravity can act on the liquid flux.
tools.usage: mt > Hygroscopic Porous Medium (hporous1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("mt").create("hporous1", "HygroscopicPorousMediumModel", 2)

parameters.name: Equilibrium between liquid and gas phases
parameters.description: Equilibrium formulation or Nonequilibrium formulation.

parameters.name: Moisture storage function / capillary pressure model
parameters.description: Sorption and capillary behavior.

parameters.name: Liquid Water / Moist Air / Porous Matrix
parameters.description: Relative permeabilities, diffusion, porosity.

tools.notes: Gravity global node appears when 'Account for gravity in liquid velocity' is selected in the interface.

tools.name: Moisture Flux and Moisture Content (Moisture Transport boundary conditions)
tools.description: Exterior boundary conditions of the Moisture Transport interfaces. Moisture Flux adds a moisture flux g0 (general), a convective flux from vapor concentration difference or from vapor pressure difference (mass transfer coefficient, e.g. from the heat and mass transfer analogy), with an option to include the latent heat of evaporation. Moisture Content constrains the vapor concentration using relative humidity plus temperature, vapor concentration or vapor mass fraction, optionally from Ambient Properties.
tools.usage: mt > Boundaries > Moisture Flux (mf1) | Moisture Content (mc1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("mt").create("mf1", "MoistureFlux", 1); ...create("mc1", "MoistureContent", 0)

parameters.name: Flux type
parameters.description: General moisture flux, Convective (concentrations difference), Convective (pressures difference).

parameters.name: Mass transfer coefficient, external humidity
parameters.description: beta and phi_w,ext / ambient.

parameters.name: Specify (Moisture Content)
parameters.description: Relative humidity + T0, vapor concentration, or vapor mass fraction.

tools.notes: A positive moisture flux adds moisture to the domain; inlet/outlet conditions are Inflow and Outflow.

tools.name: Thin Moisture Barrier and Nonequilibrium Boundary (Moisture Transport)
tools.description: Thin Moisture Barrier models a discontinuous moisture content across interior or exterior boundaries - by default a vapor barrier (vapor permeability or vapor resistance factor and thickness) - or a general barrier with a user moisture transfer coefficient beta, giving upside/downside fluxes proportional to (phi_w,d - phi_w,u). Nonequilibrium Boundary is the default node marking boundaries of Nonequilibrium Hygroscopic Porous Medium domains, where conditions must be applied through the Moist Air or Liquid Water subnodes.
tools.usage: mt > Boundaries > Thin Moisture Barrier (tmb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("mt").create("tmb1", "ThinMoistureBarrier", 1)

parameters.name: Moisture flux definition
parameters.description: Vapor barrier material properties (default) or user-defined moisture transfer coefficient.

parameters.name: Thickness, vapor resistance factor
parameters.description: Barrier properties (e.g. polyethylene foil).

tools.notes: The heat-side counterpart of a thin barrier is Thin Layer in the heat interface.

tools.name: Heat Transfer Predefined Flux and Source Variables (ht.ntflux, ht.tflux, ht.Qtot)
tools.description: Predefined variables of the Heat Transfer interfaces (prefix ht, htlsh for shells): domain fluxes ht.tflux (total), ht.dflux (conductive), ht.cflux (convective), ht.turbflux; boundary normal fluxes ht.ntflux, ht.ndflux, ht.ncflux, radiative flux ht.rflux, inward flux ht.q0; interior-boundary up/down fluxes ht.ntflux_u/_d; sources ht.Qtot, ht.Qbtot, ht.Qltot, ht.Qptot; out-of-plane fluxes ht.tflux_u/_d/_z; plus ht.Tref, damage variables ht.alpha, ht.alphanecr, ht.theta_d, thin-layer temperatures ht.Tu/ht.Td and feature-scoped values (ht.hf1.h, ht.tc1.hjoint, ht.id1.T, ht.ofl1.Tave).
tools.usage: Results > expressions such as ht.ntflux (boundary), ht.tfluxx/y/z, ht.dfluxMag, ht.gradTmag; in Derived Values > Surface Integration integrate ht.ntflux to get heat rates.

parameters.name: ht.ntflux
parameters.description: Normal total heat flux (W/m^2); integrate over boundaries for heat rate.

parameters.name: ht.tflux / ht.dflux / ht.cflux
parameters.description: Total, conductive, convective heat flux vectors.

parameters.name: ht.q0 / ht.rflux
parameters.description: Inward heat flux / radiative heat flux on boundaries.

parameters.name: ht.Qtot
parameters.description: Total domain heat source.

tools.example:
Results > Derived Values > Surface Integration on outlet: ht.ntflux (heat carried out)
Results > Arrow Volume: ht.tfluxx, ht.tfluxy, ht.tfluxz
Results > Surface: ht.Tu - ht.Td across a thin layer
tools.notes: Sign convention: ht.ntflux is positive for heat leaving the domain through the boundary normal. See 'Predefined Variables' (Heat Transfer Module User's Guide).

tools.name: Heat and Energy Balance Variables (ht.dEiInt, ht.ntfluxInt, ht.QInt, ht.heatBalance)
tools.description: Global integral variables for verifying heat and energy conservation: ht.dEiInt (total accumulated heat rate), ht.ntfluxInt (total net heat rate through exterior boundaries), ht.QInt (total heat source including boundary, edge, point and radiative sources), ht.WstrInt (stress power: pressure work plus viscous dissipation), and ht.heatBalance = dEiInt + ntfluxInt + WstrInt - QInt, which should be close to zero. The energy counterparts are ht.dEi0Int, ht.ntefluxInt, ht.WInt and ht.energyBalance (total energy including kinetic energy and work).
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values > Global Evaluation: ht.heatBalance, ht.ntfluxInt, ht.QInt (Heat Transfer > Global > Heat and energy balance in the variable menu).

parameters.name: ht.heatBalance
parameters.description: Residual of the heat balance (W).

parameters.name: ht.energyBalance
parameters.description: Residual of the energy balance (W).

parameters.name: ht.ntfluxInt / ht.ntefluxInt
parameters.description: Net heat / energy rate through exterior boundaries.

tools.notes: QInt is positive when energy is produced. A large heatBalance indicates insufficient mesh resolution or wrong boundary conditions.
